# Draft:Peter Ralston

*Fetched 2026-09-26T03:34:12Z — revision 1376596028 (https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Draft%3APeter_Ralston&oldid=1376596028). Reference copy for local comparison only; do not edit Wikipedia from this file.*

| Peter Ralston
| Nationality | American
| Style | Cheng Hsin
| Other information
| Occupation | Martial arts teacher and author

**Peter Ralston** is an American martial arts teacher and author founder of Cheng Hsin, an internal martial arts and bodywork system. In 1978, he won the light-heavyweight division at the Second World Kuoshu Martial Arts Tournament in Taiwan, according to contemporary newspaper and magazine accounts.[1][2]

The *Oakland Tribune* reported that Ralston was the first American to win a championship at the tournament.[1] A contemporary feature in *Black Belt* and later articles in *Parade* and *Blitz* described him as the first non-Asian competitor to win the event.[2][3][4]

## Early life

Ralston was born in San Francisco and spent part of his childhood in Asia, where his father worked.[3] In an interview published in the *Parade* column *Significa*, he said that a friend persuaded him to take judo classes in Singapore when he was nine. He also described a later insight into t'ai chi ch'uan and the idea that the art should not be based on struggle.[3]

Further claims about Ralston's school and university sporting achievements should be included only if they can be verified from an appropriate independent source. A USAdojo profile reports that he was a sumo champion at his high school in Japan and later a judo and fencing champion at the University of California, Berkeley.[5]

## Martial arts career

Ralston founded Cheng Hsin in 1975. A USAdojo profile states that he opened the Cheng Hsin School of Internal Martial Arts and Center for Ontological Research in Oakland, California, in 1977.[5] The founding date and institutional history should preferably be supported by an independent contemporary source.

### 1978 tournament

In 1978, Ralston won the light-heavyweight division at the Second World Kuoshu Martial Arts Tournament in Taiwan.[1]

The *Oakland Tribune* reported that Ralston was the first American to win a championship at the tournament.[1] A feature in *Black Belt* later described him as the first non-Asian competitor to win the event.[2]

A 1979 feature in the *San Francisco Chronicle* referred to Ralston as a “World martial arts champion” and described him teaching at his Cheng Hsin academy in Oakland.[6]

A 1982 article in *Parade* described Ralston as a San Francisco native and reported details about his age, height, weight, and participation in the tournament. It compared the event with the fictional martial arts contest depicted in Bruce Lee's *Enter the Dragon*.[3]

In 2011, *Blitz* published an interview with Ralston under the title “The Man Behind Bloodsport?”.[4]

## Teaching and writing

Ralston's Cheng Hsin work combines martial arts instruction with bodywork, facilitation, and studies of consciousness. His own interviews and organization-affiliated publications describe his approach as emphasizing direct experience, physical awareness, and effective interaction rather than fixed technique.[7][8]
